content:
irene: Seeing a wave of LB healthcheck failures in us-east-edge, pods getting 502s and nodes marked NotReady. Started ~10:02 UTC.
alex: which LB? external edge-lb-us-east1? any specific backend group?
irene: yes edge-lb-us-east1 -> target group tg-inference-us-east-1, health check failures for /hc on port 8080, kubelet logs show connection reset.
miguel: I can grab NACL + SG state. @sre-oncall are we doing any infra rollouts right now?
sre-oncall: no infra rollouts in the window, nothing scheduled in Terraform apply queue.
alex: quick test from one affected node: curl -v http://10.10.35.22:8080/hc -> resets after SYN. Can you try from outside (LB) to node port?
miguel: running aws cli to inspect network-acl attached to the subnet (us-east1-edge-subnet-3):

aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c3d

Got output showing a deny rule overlapping ephemeral ports:

Rule 100: DENY TCP 32768-65535 0.0.0.0/0
Rule 110: ALLOW TCP 80 0.0.0.0/0
Rule 120: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0

miguel: that DENY looks wrong — it's blocking ephemeral outbound connections and also the LB healthcheck return path.
irene: that would explain node probes and kube-proxy failing to complete session handshake.
alex: how did that rule get in? search for recent changes in Terraform state.
miguel: checking tfstate and audit logs... found a policy change rolled ~2h ago by infra-service-account: change set named "edge-nacl-tighten". The change intended to restrict incoming management ports but the rule used 32768-65535 instead of a narrower CIDR for management hosts.
miguel: CLI to remove the deny (temporary hotfix):

aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0f1e2d3c --rule-number 100 --protocol 6 --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=32768,To=65535 --egress true

alex: we should not open ephemeral to 0.0.0.0/0 long-term. For hotfix allow only the LB and k8s managed jump hosts CIDRs.
irene: applied change to allow ephemeral to the LB and k8s control plane CIDRs only. Re-running health checks.
(muted few seconds)
miguel: LB healthchecks are passing now, node readiness recovered for affected nodes.
irene: confirmed pods are coming back, 200s on /hc.
sre-oncall: filing follow-up: revert the tf change and create a targeted rule. Also adding guardrail to the CI that prevents wildcard ephemeral denies in NACLs for edge subnets.
alex: add a postmortem note: root cause = human/terraform variable mis-configuration where the intended CIDR var was empty, resulting in fallback to 0.0.0.0/0 and a broad deny. Link to runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/network/nacl-ephemeral
miguel: creating PR to update module to validate non-empty cidr and to add acceptance test against rules that deny ephemeral ranges globally.
irene: thanks everyone — moving to close once PR is merged. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3845, severity: P2, assigned: eng-infra
alex: note for oncall: consider using security-group based control for these subnets where possible (stateful) to avoid accidental stateless denies.
